source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 iunie — «Sfântul Mucenic Alexandru»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος και Αντωνίνα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and dates both «(; - 313)». It is plainly the same man: the Christian named Alexander who went into the brothel where the eparch Phystus had thrown the virgin Antonina and got her out by lending her his own clothes, was arrested with her, mutilated, smeared with pitch and burnt. The page adds that their relics were later brought to Constantinople and laid in the monastery of Maximinus, where a synaxis of them was held. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Timotei, Episcopul Prusei, al Sfinților Mucenici Alexandru și Antonina, Glasul 4 (one troparion printed for the martyrs of the day together)

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their struggles received from thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having thy strength they overthrew the tormentors and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls, O Christ God.

hymns.text: Ξυνωρὶς ἡ ἁγία τῶν Μαρτύρων ὑμνείσθω μοί, σὺν τῷ εὐκλεεῖ Ἀλεξάνδρω, Ἀντωνίνα ἡ πάνσεμνος· ἀγάπη γὰρ καὶ πίστει εὐσεβεῖ, ἐκλάμψαντες ἐν ἄθλοις ἱεροίς, ἰαμάτων ἐφαπλούσι μαρμαρυγᾶς, τοὶς ποθῶ ἀνακράζουσα δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν, πάσιν ἰάματα

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος α’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος και Αντωνίνα», and the one that names them both; the second, «Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε», is the common of martyrs

english.text: Let the holy pair of the martyrs be hymned by me — the all-modest Antonina together with the renowned Alexander; for shining out in sacred contests by love and by devout faith, they spread abroad the radiance of healings upon those who cry to them with longing: Glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who through you works healings for all.

hymns.text: Τοὺς ἐν Χριστῷ, πνευματικοὺς ὁμαίμονας, καὶ ἐν ὁδοῖς, τῆς εὐσεβείας σύμφρονας, τὸν θεόφρονα Ἀλέξανδρον, σὺν Ἀντωνίνῃ μακαρίσωμεν· τοὺς ἄθλους γὰρ ἐκείνων καὶ τὰ στίγματα, ὡς μύρον εὐωδίας προσεδέξατο, ὁ τούτους δοξάσας ὡς ηὐδόκησε.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τοὺς ἀσφαλεῖς — the second of two kontakia on the page of «Άγιοι Αλέξανδρος και Αντωνίνα», and the one that names them both; the first, «Τῶν Μαρτύρων ἔλαμψεν», is a common

english.text: Let us call blessed the godly-minded Alexander together with Antonina, kinsfolk in the spirit in Christ and of one mind upon the ways of piety; for he who glorified them as he saw fit received their contests and their wounds as myrrh of sweet fragrance.
